content: 1. Administer aztreonam intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) at a dose of 1 to 5 grams every 8 to 12 hours, ensuring the total daily dose does not exceed 8 grams. 2. For nebulized administration, use 75 mg every 8 hours for 28 days, ensuring at least 4 hours between doses. Do not repeat this regimen for another 28 days after completion. Pretreatment with a bronchodilator is recommended. 3. For the treatment of oral manifestations of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) in patients older than 9 months, administer 30 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, not exceeding 120 mg/kg/day. Safety and efficacy have not been established for patients younger than 9 months. 4. For patients older than 9 months, administer 30 mg/kg IV every 6 to 8 hours, not exceeding 120 mg/kg/day. Safety and efficacy remain unestablished for those under 9 months. 5. For patients older than 9 months, administer 50 mg/kg IV every 6 to 8 hours, not exceeding 200 mg/kg/day or 8 grams per day. 6. For patients older than 7 years, administer 75 mg via nebulizer three times daily, ensuring at least 4 hours between doses, for 28 days. Do not repeat this regimen for another 28 days. 7. Aztreonam decreases the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is complete. 8. Avoid coadministration of aztreonam with the cholera vaccine, as systemic antibiotics may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 9. Aztreonam reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 10. Aztreonam decreases the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is complete. 11. Aztreonam may reduce the levels or effects of oral conjugated estrogens, dienogest/estradiol valerate, estradiol, synthetic conjugated estrogens, estropipate, and mestranol by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, caution and monitoring are advised. Consider alternative or additional forms of birth control during concomitant use. 12. Aztreonam may increase the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Aztreonam may reduce the levels or effects of thiamine, pantothenic acid, biotin, and pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 14. Aztreonam may decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Aztreonam and aminoglycosides (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, tobramycin, neomycin, paromomycin, streptomycin) may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing their combined effects against Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacteriaceae. The clinical significance is unknown, but this combination may be used synergistically. 16. Aztreonam and beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, cefadroxil, cefamandole, cefpirome, temocillin) may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing their combined effects against Enterobacteriaceae. The clinical significance is unknown, but this combination may be used synergistically. 17. Cefotaxime may reduce the efficacy of aztreonam by inducing beta-lactamase production, which can inactivate aztreonam. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Chloramphenicol may reduce the efficacy of aztreonam due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Consider alternative therapies. 19. Probenecid may increase aztreonam levels by decreasing its elimination. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 20. Adverse effects of aztreonam include facial edema, joint swelling, chest and throat tightness, bronchospasm, skin rash, abnormal taste, anaphylaxis, anemia, angioedema, aphthous ulcers, breast tenderness, Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD), confusion, diplopia, dizziness, dyspnea, transient electrocardiographic changes, erythema multiforme, eosinophilia, fever, flushing, halitosis, headache, hepatitis, hypotension, insomnia, jaundice, and leukocytosis.
